LAREDO, Texas — More than 500 volunteers are expected to fan out across Laredo on Saturday for the 17th annual Make a Difference Day, with Texas A&M International University and Laredo College joining forces once again for one of the city’s biggest single-day service pushes, according to TAMIU.

From 9 a.m. to noon, students, faculty and staff from both schools will take on four sites along Zacate Creek, tackling trash pickup, graffiti cover-up and beautification projects aimed at restoring the creek corridor and the public spaces around it.

The effort is led by TAMIU’s Office of Student Affairs with the Student Government Association’s Leaders Organizing Volunteer Events committee, and it draws backing from community partners including the City of Laredo, the LISD Transportation Department, Nature Fresh Farms, Coca-Cola Southwest Beverages, the Rio Grande International Study Center and H-E-B. University leaders say the goal goes beyond a one-day cleanup: encouraging students to take ownership of the shared spaces their city uses every day.

Since its start in 2010, the campus-led day of service has supported causes ranging from Habitat for Humanity and the Laredo Animal Care Facility to Volunteers Serving the Need and the Ruthe B. Cowl Rehabilitation Center — a long record of students showing up for Laredo, year after year.

Anyone looking to pitch in can find details through TAMIU’s Office of Student Affairs.

Sources: Texas A&M International University announcement (Oct. 15, 2026).

title: TAMIU and Laredo College team up for 17th annual Make a Difference Day Saturday
